-def merge(ids, pair, idx):
-    """
-    In the list of integers (ids), replace all consecutive occurrences
-    of pair with the new integer token idx
-    Example: ids=[1, 2, 3, 1, 2], pair=(1, 2), idx=4 -> [4, 3, 4]
-    """
-    newids = []
-    i = 0
-    while i < len(ids):
-        # if not at the very last position AND the pair matches, replace it
-        if ids[i] == pair[0] and i < len(ids) - 1 and ids[i+1] == pair[1]:

-        else:
-            newids.append(ids[i])
-            i += 1
-    return newids
-
+def merge(ids, pair, idx):
+    """
+    In the list of integers (ids), replace all consecutive occurrences
+    of pair with the new integer token idx
+    Example: ids=[1, 2, 3, 1, 2], pair=(1, 2), idx=4 -> [4, 3, 4]
+    """
+    newids = []
+    i = 0
+    n = len(ids)
+    if n == 0:
+        return newids
+    p0 = pair[0]
+    last = n - 1
+    append = newids.append
+    while i < n:
+        # if not at the very last position AND the pair matches, replace it
+        idi = ids[i]
+        if idi == p0 and i < last and ids[i+1] == pair[1]:
+            append(idx)
+            i += 2
+        else:
+            append(idi)
+            i += 1
+    return newids
+

actions.reason: Inline the selected pair replacement in the BasicTokenizer and RegexTokenizer encode loops. Encoding already knows the selected pair and token id, so it can build the next id list directly without the extra helper call and repeated attribute lookups while preserving the same left-to-right non-overlapping merge behavior.

diff --git a/minbpe/basic.py b/minbpe/basic.py
--- a/minbpe/basic.py
+++ b/minbpe/basic.py
@@ -73,5 +73,17 @@ class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
             # if there are no more merges available, break
             if pair is None:
                 break # nothing else can be merged anymore
-            ids = merge(ids, pair, idx)
+            newids = []
+            append = newids.append
+            i = 0
+            n = len(ids)
+            p0, p1 = pair
+            while i < n:
+                if ids[i] == p0 and i < n - 1 and ids[i+1] == p1:
+                    append(idx)
+                    i += 2
+                else:
+                    append(ids[i])
+                    i += 1
+            ids = newids
         return ids

journal.text:
I tried changing minbpe.base.get_stats and minbpe.base.merge first. Then I moved the change into BasicTokenizer.encode and RegexTokenizer.encode, replacing the helper merge call inside the encode loops.

evaluation 1 was rejected. train_regex_ir worsened +5.31% with a 1% guard limit. evaluation 3 was accepted in my sandbox. train_basic_ir ratio 0.9981. train_regex_ir ratio 1.0008. encode_ir ratio 0.9029. decode_ir ratio 1.0007. save_load_ir ratio 1.0000. Outputs were identical.

I now believe the base.py helper change was the wrong place. The encode loops already have the pair and idx. Building the next id list there removes one call path without changing the left-to-right non-overlapping merge behavior.

Next, wait for the queued independent replays on the submitted encode_ir candidate. If they pass, look for the same pattern only where the caller already has pair and idx.
